p: Rabbi
raised a dilemma before Rabbi Yishmael,
son of Rabbi Yosei:
the wealthy of Eretz Yisrael,
by what
do they merit
said to him: Because they tithe, as it is stated: “A tithe you shall tithe [asser te’asser] … Take a tithe [asser] so that you will become wealthy [titasher]. … the wealthy of Babylonia, … by what

said to him: Because they tithe, as it is stated: “A tithe you shall tithe [asser te’asser] from all the crops of your seed that come out of the field each year” (Deuteronomy 14:22). The Sages interpreted this homiletically: Take a tithe [asser] so that you will become wealthy [titasher]. He asked: With regard to the wealthy of Babylonia, who are not obligated to tithe, by what
do they merit
said to him:
Because they honor the Torah

p: The Exilarch said to Rav Hamnuna:
What
which is written,
“The holy one of God is honored”
said to him:
That is Yom Kippur,
when there is no eating or drinking,
Torah said:
Honor it with a clean garment.
“And you shall honor it,” Rav said: … To … make … earlier … And Shmuel said: … To … make … later,

“And you shall honor it,” Rav said: To honor Shabbat, make the Shabbat feast earlier than on other days, in order to show that one delights in eating it. And Shmuel said: To honor Shabbat, make the Shabbat feast later,
The sons of Rav Pappa bar Abba said to Rav Pappa: … like us,
The sons of Rav Pappa bar Abba said to Rav Pappa: People like us,
for whom meat and wine is found … every day, … in what … can we change it
for whom meat and wine is found on our table every day, in what manner can we change it
said to them:
If you are accustomed to … early, … make it later
If you are accustomed to eating your meal early, make it later
if you are accustomed to making it late, … make it earlier … In the summer,
if you are accustomed to making it late, make it earlier on Shabbat. This difference will underscore the uniqueness of Shabbat. The Gemara relates: In the summer,
Rav Sheshet would seat the Sages
where the sun would reach;
in the winter,
he would seat the Sages … where the shade would reach. … so … they would stand quickly
he would seat the Sages in a place where the shade would reach. He did this so that they would stand quickly
